theory: The corpus is a registry of mathematical statements with stable identities, source occurrences, and a human review lifecycle. Content hashes identify what was stated and reviewed separately from measurements over it. Retirement preserves citation history instead of freeing names for reuse.
instead_of: A benchmark input list could contain only prompts and answers, but would not explain classification-dependent review invalidation or why deleted identifiers must remain retired records.

absorption.rationale: Occurrences, fixture-content changes, and retirement fit naturally; unresolved conjectures require changing the binary expected-value and true/false-twin model.

world_mapping.rationale: Occurrence locators, review identity, classification, and append-only issuance directly model mathematical provenance and curation.

abstraction.rationale: Entry/ProblemSet validation and separate statement, prompt, and fixture identities represent distinct reasons evidence becomes stale.

justification.rationale: Code explains malformed antecedence locators, classification-bound review, and comparison against prior issuance; tests exercise declaration assembly and command injection.

honest_limits.rationale: Mechanical validation is explicitly insufficient for faithful classification, and missing witness/provenance requires an explanation.

rehearsals.requirement: Record a second textbook occurrence of a result.
rehearsals.why: Append an Occurrence while retaining the statement identity.

rehearsals.requirement: Change a shared fixture without invalidating fixture-free conditions.
rehearsals.why: Resolved fixture contents have a separate digest component.

rehearsals.requirement: Curate unresolved conjectures beside known true/false examples.
rehearsals.why: Expected truth is binary and false twins must reference true entries; unknown truth needs an additional lifecycle/model rather than an ordinary Entry value.
